text:
Alex (Sales): Quick thread — new POC with FinEdge. Customer wants assurances on EU-only processing, wants routing pinned to eu-west and eu-central, and a sub-processor list for auditors. Can we scope what’s doable for a short-term POC?
Mira (SE): Hey Alex — doable but need to call out a couple caveats: hosted API has regional endpoints, but tenant pinning for short POCs requires us to spin a dedicated routing rule (no dedicated infra). Latency and cost tradeoffs.
Mira (SE): Can you confirm expected qps and whether they need BYOK/KMS? Those affect timeline.
Alex (Sales): They expect ~20 r/s peak, BYOK not required for POC, but they want list of subprocessors + whether any inference traffic leaves EU egress.
Jen (Legal): For the subproc list — we can provide current cloud infra subprocessors (GCP/azure regions) + third-party logging/monitoring vendors. Need to be explicit about transient edge caches and CDN providers. I'll prepare a statement.
Sam (SRE): Note: our smart routing may route to eu-west1 or eu-central1 depending on capacity. For strict eu-only, we can set a policy: route_preference = "region_pin: [eu-west1, eu-central1]" and fail closed to 429/503 if no capacity. That needs ops approval for a per-tenant policy.
Mira (SE): Adding config example we can share with the customer for the POC (they like seeing config):
```
routing_policy:
  mode: pin-list
  regions: [eu-west1, eu-central1]
  fallback: none   # fail if no matching capacity
  cache_scope: regional
```

Mira (SE): Also FYI: prefix/KV cache may still replicate small metadata for routing health checks — Jen, is that okay to call out as "control-plane metadata may go to global control plane"?
Jen (Legal): Call that out. Provide a short paragraph: "Inference payloads and models are processed in EU regions only. Control-plane metadata (routing, metrics) may be transmitted to our control plane hosted in the US; we treat it as operational telemetry and it is covered by our DPA/subprocessor controls." I'll draft.
Alex (Sales): Great. Timeline — can we have the subproc list + the routing config + a note about fail-closed option by EOD tomorrow? Customer needs it for compliance review.
Sam (SRE): EOD is tight but doable for the config + ops notes. For subproc list Jen will have to confirm, but I can produce the network path doc and expected cost delta for pinned routing (extra egress + lower bin-packing -> ~12–18% cost uplift estimate).
Jen (Legal): I'll pull together the subproc list and the compliance blurb. Two asks: (1) confirm we are not enabling BYOK for POC, (2) confirm that they accept fail-closed behavior (we should record that in the SOW).
Alex (Sales): Confirmed: no BYOK for the POC, customer prefers fail-closed. I'll get them to sign a short riser SOW.
OpsBot: @channel Routing rule request created: RR-3219. Owner: Sam (SRE). ETA: 48h if there are no additional infra changes.
Mira (SE): I'll draft a short runbook for the POC showing request headers, which regional endpoint to call, and an example curl:
```
curl -X POST https://eu-west1.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```

Alex (Sales): Perfect. I'll assemble a single zip for the customer: subproc list (Jen), routing config & runbook (Mira), cost uplift note & routing ticket (Sam). Will ping legal for the SOW signature after Jen's blurb.
Sam (SRE): One more thing — if they ask about disaster recovery: we can offer cross-region standby but that violates eu-only for failover. We should include an explicit choice: "strict eu-only (fail-closed)" vs "eu-primary with cross-border standby (failover)" + pricing.
Alex (Sales): Good call. I'll surface that as an option in the email. Thanks all.
Jen (Legal): Uploading subproc list draft to the shared drive, will ping when done.
Mira (SE): I'll prepare the runbook & example requests by tomorrow morning.
Alex (Sales): Closing loop — will update this thread when customer signs the riser SOW. :thumbsup:
